about.title: About the project
about.body:
Hello everyone!
I'd like to share a bit of the story — how it all started.

Once, a few years ago, I came across a phrase in a book that touched me deeply:

“If all people in the world sent out one thought at the same time — for just one minute — much could be changed.”

I encountered these words in different sources — in the books of Anastasia Novykh, in the works of Alexander Georgievich Bakaev, and also in an interview with the Elders of Mount Athos. Each mention felt like a reminder: there is great power in the unity of minds and hearts.

This is how the idea was born — to create a tool that would help each person not just dream about change, but bring it to life. A tool to improve your own life, help your loved ones, and contribute to the world — even if in small, gentle ways. Perhaps to stop a war, prevent disasters… because everything begins with a person’s inner state.

This app appeared from that intent. It was created so you can mark your kind actions, observe the collective movement, and see how together we create harmony and light.

How to Use the App.
Here’s a brief overview of how it works. Every eight hours, when the timer reaches zero, a three-minute "Rainbow Window" opens. This is a special slot—short but powerful—when you should select Live mode and launch your thought-form. Press the button and keep a calm, confident focus for one full minute.

Focus on your core intention:
— to ask for peace instead of war,
— to protect the Earth from disasters,
— to support your loved ones and those nearby,
— to help yourself and strengthen your health.

When the window ends, it will close and your contribution will be counted in the overall statistics—you’ll see how small personal efforts add up to a shared impulse. If you didn’t make it in time, no worries: the next "Rainbow Window" will start in eight hours. You can enable reminders in Telegram so you don’t miss the windows.

Try it. Help. Move toward the Light.
Everything is possible — when there is faith in the heart and God is near.

With love and respect,
Yaroslav and Borys.
